title: View the Ontology
description: Open Ontology and browse the different concepts.
annotation: In the navbar, open Ontology and browse the different terminology. Terms are grouped together as concepts. For example, Capability lists the names, codes, categories, roles etc. that characterise a Capability.

title: Propose a new code
description: Add a new code under a concept type.
annotation: Under the concept type, enter a code and a label, then choose Add / Save. A new code is a proposal until the Ontology Manager approves it. Approval is not part of this demo: the Ontology Manager reviews each proposed code and decides whether it becomes canonical.

title: Find the pending code
description: Open Ontology Approvals and find the pending code.
annotation: In the navbar, open Ontology, then Approvals, and find the code you proposed. This is where the Ontology Manager decides which codes become canonical.

title: Approve the code
annotation: Choose Accept on the pending code. Acceptance makes the code canonical, so Packs that use it can be published.

title: Reject the code
description: Reject a pending code with a reason.
annotation: Choose Reject on the pending code, enter what needs to change and choose Confirm reject. A rejected code is not canonical, and the comment tells the author what to change.

title: Compose a code from an existing code
description: Compose a code from an existing code.
annotation: Choose Compose, select the source code, choose specialization or override, enter the new code and choose Compose. A composed code builds on an existing one, so the vocabulary grows without starting again.

title: Ontology provides the semantic foundation for the platform
annotation: Ontology defines the shared semantic vocabulary used by a Software Engineering Unit (SEU). Its purpose is to ensure that all Participants, Deliverables, Knowledge, Evidence, Decisions and Packs operate using a common understanding of engineering concepts. Tenants can override Platform Ontology or define new ones. Demo does not allow this feature.

title: The Registry lists every declared Pack
description: Find the Pack in the Registry - note
annotation: A Pack carries the practice an organisation chooses to follow. A Template / Profile selects the Packs it uses.

title: Find the Pack in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Pack Registry, and find the Pack.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Pack Registry. Packs are grouped into different categories. You can also view them grouped in different states. Packs can contribute to Capabilites, Services etc. They can also be declared as independent behaviors that can be added to Templates/Profiles. **Example**: - C Engineering Practices Pack contributes to "Constructing software systems " and "Reviewing engineering work " Capabilities. - Banking, Payments & Capital Markets Domain Practices Pack is an independent Pack that can be added to any Template/Profile used for delivering software in the Banking domain.

title: A Pack is the **fundamental unit of extension** within the Platform.
annotation: Packs enable organisations to include specific engineering practices, standards, policies, business domains, technologies, compliance requirements and integration environments while preserving architectural stability of the SEU.

title: Open Pack Authoring
description: Open SDK / Pack Authoring and choose New Pack.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Pack Authoring. Choose New Pack. Enter the details. Validate Pack ensures the created Pack complies to the Schema so it can be converted to a computable configuration.

title: A new Pack starts as a Draft
annotation: A Pack is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published.

title: Create the draft
description: Enter code, name, category, version and classification, then create the draft.
annotation: Enter a code, a name, a category, a version and an installation classification. Choose Create draft. A new Pack starts as a Draft. Use Save draft for later changes.

title: Contributions give the Pack its content
annotation: Contributions are the checklists, Obligations and other definitions that a Pack adds. You can add this in the form or import as a  JSON document.

title: Add the contributions
description: Paste a Pack document into the JSON import card and import it.
annotation: Add the contributions in the form, or paste a JSON document into the JSON import card and choose Import. An import replaces the whole document. If you want this Pack to be part of a competency and be reused elsewhere, add the Capability this should be part of. For example, you are creating a new ESLint, add it to the "Development" Capability. You can now define your Checklists and Quality Gates in the Pack. Remember to include this in the Profile you choose for your engineering work.

title: A Pack can be composed from existing Packs
annotation: Composition builds a new Pack from existing Packs by a Composition Strategy, such as Specialization (an exact copy of one parent), Merge, Union or Override. The result is a starting point for the draft, not a lock.

title: Compose the Pack from source Packs
description: Choose a Composition Strategy and the source Pack(s) on the draft, save, then choose Compose from sources.
annotation: On the draft, choose a Composition Strategy and one or more source Packs, and save. Then choose Compose from sources. The draft is pre-filled from the sources. Review the result and edit it as needed.

title: Validation checks the Pack before it is published
annotation: Validation checks that the Pack is complete and consistent. A Pack with a new code waits at Validated until the Ontology accepts the code.

title: Validate the Pack
annotation: Save the draft, then choose Validate Pack at the bottom of the page. Validation checks that the Pack is complete and consistent and moves it to Validated.

title: Publishing makes the Pack available
annotation: A Pack moves one state at a time: Validated, Published, then Active. Only an Active Pack can be selected by a Profile.

title: Publish the Pack
annotation: Choose Publish Pack to move the Pack to Published. Then choose Activate Pack to make it Active so that a Profile can select it.

title: A Template is the engineering blueprint for delivering software
description: Find the Template in the Registry - note
annotation: A Template groups the typical processes that a type of work needs, such as the domain, compliance and technology Packs. A Profile is built on a Template. Templates declare structures combining Capabilities to create a typical software engineering configuration.

title: Find the Template in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Templates and find the Template.
annotation: ArchVault Digital Shelf is being built for mobiles. Check the Template Registry for a mobile platform development Template. In the navbar, open Registry, then Template Registry. Search for "mobile". You will see there are 2 Templates: One defined by the Platform and the other by Demo tenant.

title: Explore the two Templates in the Registry
description: View the Templates to identify the differences.
annotation: View the "Mobile Application" declared by the Platform. Go to the Deliverable Catalogue tab. You can see the Deliverables to be created for this blueprint. You can also see the Deliverable dependency. Demo has created its own lean version of the Template. View the "Mobile Application" declared by the Demo tenant. Go to the Deliverable Catalogue tab. You can see the Template has three Deliverables and no dependencies.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Template
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Template. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Template
description: Copy an existing Template into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Template. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: Authoring is where a Template is declared
annotation: Template Authoring is where an organisation declares the Template for its own type of work. The Registry lists the Templates already declared.

title: Open Template Authoring
description: Open SDK / Template Authoring and choose New Template.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Template Authoring. Choose New Template.

title: A new Template starts as a Draft
annotation: A Template is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published.

title: Create the draft
description: Enter the Template details and create the draft.
annotation: Enter a code, a name and a version for the Template. Choose Create draft. A new Template starts as a Draft.

title: The Packs make up the Template
annotation: The Packs selected here define the practice the Template carries. A Pack declares the practice. The Template chooses which Packs apply.

title: Select the Packs
description: Select the Packs the Template composes and save the draft.
annotation: On the draft, select the Packs for each category, such as domain, compliance and technology. Choose Save.

title: Validation checks the Template before it is published
annotation: Validation checks that the Template is complete and its Packs are compatible.

title: Validate the Template
annotation: Save the draft, then choose Validate Template. Validation checks that the Template is complete and consistent.

title: Publishing makes the Template available
annotation: A Template moves one state at a time: Validated, Published, then Active. An Active Template can be used by a Profile.

title: Publish the Template
annotation: Choose Publish Template, then Activate Template. An Active Template can be used by a Profile.

title: A Profile tailors a Template for the project needs
description: Find the Profile in the Registry - note
annotation:
Templates are very broad. Profiles use the Templates and tailor it for use.

Profiles specify environments, configurations, authority mechanisms etc. These are local to the project. To reflect it, a Profile has to be derived from the Template and specifics included.

The Demo created a default Profile "ArchVault Digital App"for the ArchVault team.

title: Find the Profile in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Profiles, and find the Profile.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Profile Registry. Search for "ArchVault Digital App". You can view the engineering parameters for the profile. Let us suppose you want to have a different Profile. You can create one or copy an existing one to modify.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Profile
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to declare a Profile. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published. To view your draft, go to SDK Authoring and Profile Authoring.

title: Copy the Profile
description: Copy an existing Profile into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Profile. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing. Let us give it a name "Modified Demo Profile for ArchVault Team." You can modify other fields and choose Save draft.

title: Edit the Profile
annotation: Let us add some specific configurations for the ArchVault development. Go to the Deliverable Catalogue. You can see three deliverables are defined which are derived from the base Template. We will create the deliverable dependencies.

title: Edit the Deliverable dependencies
annotation: Go to the Dependency Graph in the Deliverable Catalogue. 1. Choose "Deployment Manifest" in To code, "Requirements Analysis Model" and Required State as "In Progress" for the first set. 2. Choose "Source Code" in To code, "Requirements Analysis Model" and Required State as "Approved" for the second set. 3. Remove the third set. 4. Save the Draft and provide the reason for editing if it asks for one. You should see the updated dependency graph for the Deliverables.

title: Edit the Service Levels
annotation: Go to the Parameter Overrides tab. You can override Service levels that the Template defines. For example, Functional correctness of Source Code is expected to be at least 90 percent. You can relax this to 75 percent or tighten it to 95 percent. The Service levels are measured and reported in Telemetry automatically.

title: Authoring is where a Profile is declared
annotation: Profile Authoring is where an organisation declares the Profile for its own team. The Registry lists the Profiles already declared.

title: Open Profile Authoring
description: Open SDK / Profile Authoring and choose New Profile.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Profile Authoring. Choose New Profile.

title: A new Profile starts as a Draft
annotation: A Profile is created as a Draft. It has no effect until it is validated and published.

title: Create the draft
description: Enter the Profile details and create the draft.
annotation: Enter a code, a name and a version for the Profile. Choose Create draft. A new Profile starts as a Draft.

title: The Packs make up the Profile
annotation: The Packs selected here define the practice the Profile applies. A Pack declares the practice. The Profile chooses which Packs apply.

title: Select the Packs
description: Select the Packs the Profile uses and save the draft.
annotation: On the draft, select the Packs for each category, such as domain, compliance and technology, and the optional Packs. Choose Save.

title: A Profile can set a service level
annotation: A service level states the target a Service is held to, such as a response time. The Profile can set it for the team without changing the Pack.

title: Change the service level
description: Set the service level on the Profile and save.
annotation: On the draft, set the service level for the Service and choose Save.

title: Validation checks the Profile before it is published
annotation: Validation checks that the Profile is complete and its Packs are compatible.

title: Validate the Profile
annotation: Save the draft, then choose Validate Profile. Validation checks that the Profile is complete and consistent.

title: Publishing makes the Profile available
annotation: A Published Profile is no longer editable. It has to be Activated before SEUs can use it.

title: Publish the Profile
annotation: Choose Publish Profile, then Activate Profile. An Active Profile can be used to commission a Software Engineering Unit. Activate the Profile and we will use "Modified Demo Profile for ArchVault Team" to commission an SEU in the Commission stage.

title: Engineering competencies are available in the Capability, Service and Deliverable Registry.
description: Find the Capability Definition in the Registry - note
annotation:
Capabilities represent the engineering competencies required to deliver software within a Software Engineering Unit (SEU).

A Capability defines **what engineering function must be performed**, independent of who or what performs it.

A Capability provides a guaranteed Service which includes the expected Deliverables and Service Levels.

title: Find the Capability Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry and view the Capability Definitions.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Capability Registry. Each card shows the Capability Definition and links to the Service it provides.

title: View "Designing Software Architecture" Capability
description: Search and view the Capability Definitions.
annotation: Scroll to locate or search for Designing Software Architecture and choose View. You can view the details. Choose View the Service offered to see the value the competency promises to deliver. The Roles and Worktypes section lists the Roles performing the activities in the Capability and the typical Worktypes they produce.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Capability Definition
annotation: A published Capability cannot be edited. Copying is the quickest way to define a new Capability Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be edited before it is published. A new Capability can also be created from scratch. A new Capability needs a new code. The code must be an approved Ontology concept before the Capability can be published. Also create/assign the corresponding Role, WorkType, Service and Deliverables to complete the definition.

title: Copying and editing a Capability
annotation: Let us try to create a copy of "Designing software architecture Capability".

title: Copy the Capability Definition
description: Copy a Capability Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Capability Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: Edit the Capability Definition
annotation: Make edits to the definition. There are help texts to guide you on the fields. You can save the draft. Saved drafts can be viewed on the Registry and edited further till you publish. Demo does not allow publishing of new Capability.

title: A new Capability Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Capability Definition - note
annotation: A Capability Definition is created as a draft. It has no effect until it is validated, published and activated. It is Active only after the last step.

title: Author a new Capability Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Capability Definition in SDK / Capability Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Capability Authoring. Choose New Capability, enter the details and choose Create draft. Then save, and choose Validate Capability, Publish Capability and Activate Capability in turn.

title: The Registry lists every Deliverable Definition
description: Find the Deliverable Definition in the Registry - note
annotation: A Deliverable Definition declares a kind of work product, such as a specification or a design, that a Software Engineering Unit produces.

title: Find the Deliverable Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Deliverable Registry, and find the Deliverable Definition.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Deliverable Registry. Each card shows the Deliverable Definition and its version.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Deliverable Definition
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Deliverable Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Deliverable Definition
description: Copy a Deliverable Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Deliverable Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Deliverable Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Deliverable Definition - note
annotation: A Deliverable Definition is created as a draft. It has no effect until it is validated, published and activated. It is Active only after the last step.

title: Author a new Deliverable Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Deliverable Definition in SDK / Deliverable Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Deliverable Authoring. Choose New Deliverable, enter the details and choose Create draft. Then save, and choose Validate Deliverable, Publish Deliverable and Activate Deliverable in turn.

title: The Registry lists every Service Definition
description: Find the Service Definition in the Registry - note
annotation: A Service Definition declares a service that a Software Engineering Unit offers or consumes, with its service levels.

title: Find the Service Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Service Registry, and find the Service Definition.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Service Registry. Each card shows the Service Definition and its version.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Service Definition
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Service Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Service Definition
description: Copy a Service Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Service Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Service Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Service Definition - note
annotation: A Service Definition is created as a draft. It has no effect until it is validated, published and activated. It is Active only after the last step.

title: Author a new Service Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Service Definition in SDK / Service Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Service Authoring. Choose New Service, enter the details and choose Create draft. Then save, and choose Validate Service, Publish Service and Activate Service in turn.

title: The Registry lists every Policy Definition
description: Find the Policy Definition in the Registry - note
annotation: A Policy Definition declares a rule that applies across Packs, such as a limit or a required check.

title: Find the Policy Definition in the Registry
description: Open Registry, then Policy Registry, and find the Policy Definition.
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Policy Registry. Each card shows the Policy Definition and its version.

title: Copying starts a new Draft from an existing Policy Definition
annotation: Copy is the quickest way to derive a Policy Definition. The new Draft starts with the same content and can be changed before it is published.

title: Copy the Policy Definition
description: Copy a Policy Definition into a new draft.
annotation: Choose Copy on the Policy Definition. A new Draft is created from it and opens for editing.

title: A new Policy Definition starts as a Draft
description: Author a new Policy Definition - note
annotation: A Policy Definition is created as a draft. It has no effect until it is validated, published and activated. It is Active only after the last step.

title: Author a new Policy Definition
description: Create, save, validate and publish a Policy Definition in SDK / Policy Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Policy Authoring. Choose New Policy, enter the details and choose Create draft. Then save, and choose Validate Policy, Publish Policy and Activate Policy in turn.

title: A Transition Definition declares one state change
description: Author a new Transition Definition - note
annotation: A Transition Definition declares one move from one state to another for an entity, and the authority needed to make it. It is added directly to the Current Transition Definitions and has no draft.

title: Add a Transition Definition
description: Add a Transition Definition in SDK / Transition Definition Authoring.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring and choose Transition Definition Authoring. Under Current Transition Definitions choose the Noun, enter the From and To states, choose the Verb and the Required Policies, then choose Add.

title: A schema describes the fields of a definition
description: Find the schemas in the Schema Registry - note
annotation: The Schema Registry lists the schema for each kind of definition. The authoring forms are built from these schemas.

title: Find the schemas in the Schema Registry
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Schema Registry. Each schema describes the fields of one kind of definition.

title: Participants are the people and systems that do the work
annotation: A Participant is a person or a system that can fulfil a Capability. The Registry lists the Participants available to the tenant.

title: Find the Participants
annotation: In the navbar, open Registry, then Participant Registry. Each entry is a person or system that can be given work.

title: A noun names what authority applies to
annotation: Authority is expressed as a noun and a verb, such as pack and publish. The noun is the entity. The verb is the action.

title: Open the authority nouns
description: Open the Nouns tab of the authority pages.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring, choose Transition Definition Authoring and then the Work outcome tab (Nouns). A noun names a kind of entity that authority applies to.

title: A new noun extends the authority vocabulary
annotation: A noun added here can be combined with the verbs to form a badge.

title: Add a noun
annotation: On the Nouns tab, enter the code, the label and the description, and choose Add noun.

title: A verb names an action
annotation: The verb is the action a badge permits, such as define, approve or publish.

title: Open the authority verbs
description: Open the Verbs tab of the authority pages.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring, choose Transition Definition Authoring and then the Work process tab (Verbs). A verb names an action that authority permits.

title: A new verb extends the authority vocabulary
annotation: A verb added here can be combined with the nouns to form a badge.

title: Add a verb
annotation: On the Verbs tab, enter the code, the label and the description, and choose Add verb.

title: The mapping pairs a noun with a verb
description: Open the noun and verb mapping - note
annotation: Each pairing is a badge. The mapping states which verbs are allowed for which noun, and whether a person or the platform triggers them.

title: Open the noun and verb mapping
description: Open the Mapping tab of the authority pages.
annotation: In the navbar, open SDK / Authoring, choose Transition Definition Authoring and then the Mapping tab. Each row pairs a noun with an allowed verb and shows whether the transition is Manual or Governed.

title: A new mapping creates a badge
description: Map a verb to a noun - note
annotation: Mapping a verb to a noun creates the badge that permits that action on that entity.

title: Map a verb to a noun
description: Map a verb to a noun.
annotation: On the Mapping tab, choose a noun and a verb, choose the trigger and choose Allow.

title: The trigger states who starts the transition
description: Change the trigger of a mapping - note
annotation: A Manual trigger means a person starts the transition. A Governed trigger means the platform does.

title: Change the trigger of a mapping
description: Change the trigger of a mapping.
annotation: On the Mapping tab, choose Edit on a mapping that has wired transitions, change the trigger and choose Save.

title: A transition definition declares one state change
annotation: It names the entity, the state it moves from and to, and the badge needed to make the move.

title: Open a transition definition
annotation: Open a transition definition from the list to see the states it moves between and the authority it needs.

title: Editing changes how an entity may move
annotation: A change here changes which badge is needed for a state change, and what the change triggers.

title: Edit a transition definition
description: Edit a transition definition and save.
annotation: Choose Edit, change the definition and choose Save.

title: A badge gives a user the authority to act
description: Grant a badge to a user - note
annotation: A user can make a state change only when they hold the badge it needs. The Tenant Administrator grants badges to users.

title: Grant a badge to a user
description: Open Tenant User Management and grant badges to a user.
annotation: In the user menu at the top right, open Tenant User Management. In the row of a user, select the badges and choose Save.

title: An Objective states what the work is for
annotation: An Objective states aspects of the software you want to build. Objectives are built as a hierarchy. One or more Software Engineering Units are commissioned to deliver the Objectives.

title: Find the Objectives
annotation: Demo has already built the Objectives for the ArchVault Digital Shelf. In the navbar, open SEU Platform. From here, click on the Objectives. The list shows the Objectives and where each sits in the hierarchy.

title: A new Objective starts as a proposal
annotation: The Objective waits in its first state, Defined, until a person with the authority activates it.

title: Propose an Objective
description: Choose New under a parent Objective, enter the details and create it.
annotation: On the Objectives page choose New Strategic Objective, or use the plus button of a tier on an existing Objective to add a child. Enter the details and create it. A new Objective is in the Defined state until it is activated.

title: Objectives hierarchy
annotation: A larger outcome is broken into smaller realisable Objectives. Strategic Objective is split into multiple Operational Objectives. Each Operational Objective holds many Engineering Objectives.

title: Open an Objective
annotation: Choose View on an Objective in the list to see its details and its child Objectives. You can edit the Objective, add Objectives and build the hierarchy as long as it is in the Defined state.

title: An Objective can be refined
annotation: The statement and the required Capabilities can be edited only while the Objective is in the Defined state. Submit sends the revision for validation. Save keeps it without a new version.

title: Edit the Objective
annotation: Open the Objective and choose Edit Objective. Change the statement or the required Capabilities, then choose Submit or Save.

title: Moving changes where an Objective sits
annotation: The Objective keeps its content and takes a new place in the hierarchy. Its whole subtree moves with it.

title: Move the Objective
description: Move the Objective under another parent.
annotation: On the Edit page of the Objective, open Move to a Different Parent, select the new parent and choose Move. A Strategic Objective has no parent, so it cannot be moved.

title: Comments record the discussion
annotation: Comments stay with the Objective so that later readers can see why it changed. A comment can be added in any state.

title: Comment on the Objective
annotation: On the Edit page of the Objective, enter the comment under Comments and choose Post.

title: Activate is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Activation makes the Objective current. A Software Engineering Unit can then be commissioned for it. Demo allows you to create and edit Objectives. You may not be able to activate them.

title: Activate the Objective
annotation: On the Objective page, choose Transition to Active. Only a person holding the activation badge sees the button.

title: Supersede is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Supersession replaces an Objective with a newer one. The old Objective stays on record.

title: Supersede the Objective
annotation: On an Active Objective, choose Supersede. Select the Objective that replaces it, or choose the link to create a new one, then choose Supersede in the dialog.

title: Retire is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Retirement ends an Active Objective that is no longer pursued. The Objective and its subtree are retired and keep their history.

title: Retire the Objective
annotation: On an Active Objective, choose Retire Objective & subtree and confirm.

title: Archive is a state change of the Objective
annotation: Archiving is the last state of an Objective that is achieved, superseded or retired. It stays on record.

title: Archive the Objective
annotation: On an achieved, superseded or retired Objective, choose Transition to Archived.

title: Reject is a state change of the Objective
annotation: An Active Objective that will not go ahead is rejected, with a reason. Rejected Objectives are listed on the Rejected tab of the Objectives page.

title: Reject the Objective
annotation: On an Active Objective, enter the reason in the Reject box and choose Reject. The reason is required.

title: Only a Defined leaf can be deleted
annotation: An Objective with no children that is still in the Defined state has not been acted on and can be deleted. Once an Objective has moved on, it is retired or archived instead.

title: Delete a Defined Objective
description: Delete a leaf Objective that is in the Defined state.
annotation: Open a leaf Objective in the Defined state, choose Delete Objective and confirm.

title: Commissioning has preconditions
description: Check the Objective is ready to commission - note
annotation: An Objective is commissioned only when it is active and its Template and Profile are in place.

title: Check the Objective is ready to commission
description: Check the Objective is ready to commission.
annotation: After the SEU is saved, choose Validate in the Saved SEU section. The Commission Validation page checks that the Objective, Profile, Template and everything they reference are still live, and lists each check as Live or Dead.

title: The Engineering Behavior Model is composed from Packs
description: Compose the Engineering Behavior Model - note
annotation: Composition joins the Packs of the Template and Profile into the model that governs the Software Engineering Unit.

title: Compose the Engineering Behavior Model
description: Compose the Engineering Behavior Model for the Objective.
annotation: On the Commission Validation page choose Compose EBM. The Compose EBM page shows what the Template and Profile resolve to, the Packs they compose and any conflicts.

title: A Software Engineering Unit does the work
description: Find the Software Engineering Units - note
annotation: A Software Engineering Unit is commissioned for an Objective. It carries the Engineering Behavior Model defined for the SEU and tracks it through its execution.

title: Find the Software Engineering Units
annotation: In the navbar, open SEU Platform, then All SEUs. Look at the SEU that is in operational state. You can see and control execution by going through View. If you just want a dashboard view, click on EEG Follow steps in Commission tab to get an operational SEU to follow along.

title: Commissioning creates the unit
description: Commission a Software Engineering Unit - note
annotation:
Commissioning defines the Engineering Configuration that is followed for creating the software to achieve the Objective.

Commissioning is done by attaching a Profile to an Objective and making the SEU operational.

title: Commission a Software Engineering Unit
description: Choose New SEU, select the Objective, Template and Profile, and commission.
annotation: Find an Active Engineering Objective that has no SEU. In the Objectives tree, open its Options menu and choose Commission SEU. On the Objective page the button reads Commission an SEU from this Objective. If an SEU already exists, the menu shows Commissioned — view SEU. Choose the Profile "Modified Demo Profile for ArchVault Team" and choose Save. The Saved SEU section then offers Validate. Validation checks that the Packs and Profiles used are still Active. Compose the Engineering Behavior Model by choosing Compose EBM on the validation page.

title: Resolve EBM conflicts
annotation: The Engineering Behavior Model is composed from the Template, Profile, Packs and Policies. Their directions can conflict. When the model is composed, the conflicts are listed and the user resolves them. The SEU does not complete Commissioning until the conflicts are resolved.

title: Resolve the Engineering Behavior Model conflicts
description: Resolve the conflicts of the composed Engineering Behavior Model.
annotation: Go to All SEUs. When the SEU has no Engineering Behavior Model yet, choose Compose. On the compose page choose Resolve Conflicts. In the Services tab, choose "Mobile Engineering Service", tick the Work Item Types within each Deliverable and choose Apply. In the Capabilities tab, include or exclude the Packs listed, then choose Apply. When no conflict is open, choose Validate. Then choose View EBM and choose Activate at the top of the EBM page. Back in All SEUs, the SEU becomes operational.

title: The Deliverable tab
description: Open a Software Engineering Unit Deliverable tab - note
annotation: The Deliverable tab shows the Deliverables state in execution. It shows the Deliverable dependency, the participants assigned to them, the Quality Gate checks and what blocks them from progressing.

title: Open a Software Engineering Unit
annotation: a. Deployment Manifest and Source Code Deliverables are dependent on Requirements Analysis Model in the Approved State

title: The unit page shows the whole picture
description: Open a Software Engineering Unit - note
annotation: The page shows the unit's state and what it must deliver, who is working on it and what is outstanding.

title: Open a Software Engineering Unit
annotation: Choose View on a unit in the list to see its state, Capabilities, Deliverables and Obligations.

title: A unit has a lifecycle
description: Move the unit to its next state - note
annotation: A unit moves through states such as validated, suspended and retired. Each move needs the matching badge.

title: Move the unit to its next state
description: Move the SEU to its next lifecycle state.
annotation: On the unit page, choose one of the buttons offered, such as Validate, Suspend, Resume, Retire or Archive. Only the buttons the viewer holds the badge for are shown.

title: The model governs the unit
description: Open the Engineering Behavior Model - note
annotation: The Engineering Behavior Model is authoritative for the unit until it is superseded through a governed recomposition.

title: Open the Engineering Behavior Model
description: Open the Engineering Behavior Model of the SEU.
annotation: Choose View EBM on the unit page, or in the All SEUs list. The page shows the Metadata, the composed Packs and one tab for each settled table, such as Services, Capabilities and Policies. The link appears once the SEU has an Engineering Behavior Model.

title: The model is validated and then activated
description: Move the model to its next state - note
annotation: Activation makes the model the one the unit follows.

title: Move the model to its next state
description: Move the Engineering Behavior Model to its next state.
annotation: At the top of the EBM page, choose Validate, then Activate.

title: A Capability is fulfilled by a Participant
annotation: The Participant takes on the Capability and can then be given work.

title: Fulfil a Capability
description: Fulfil a Capability with a Participant.
annotation: On the Capability Fulfilment tab of the unit page, tick the Participants offered for a Capability and choose Assign.

title: A Participant can be replaced
annotation: The work stays with the Capability. A different Participant takes over.

title: Replace the Participant
description: Replace the Participant on a Capability.
annotation: Choose Replace beside the Participant and select another.

title: Release returns the Capability to the pool
annotation: The Capability is Unfulfilled again until another Participant is assigned.

title: Release a Capability
annotation: On the Capability Fulfilment tab, tick the assigned Participants of a Fulfilled Capability and choose Replace. They are released and you then pick the replacements.

title: Work is queued for Participants
annotation: The queue lists what has to be done next. Work is generated from the Engineering Behavior Model.

title: Open the work queue
description: Open the work queue of the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, open the work queue. It lists the work items waiting for a Participant.

title: Completing work moves the unit forward
annotation: A completed item can release the next item and update the state of the Deliverable or Obligation it belongs to.

title: Complete a work item
annotation: Choose Complete on a work item.

title: A Deliverable has a lifecycle
annotation: A Deliverable is a work product. It moves from draft through review to approval.

title: Move a Deliverable on
description: Move a Deliverable to its next state.
annotation: On the unit page, choose a state change on a Deliverable.

title: An Obligation is something the unit must satisfy
annotation: An Obligation moves through analysis, work, resolution, verification and closure, each with its own badge.

title: Move an Obligation on
description: Move an Obligation to its next state.
annotation: On the unit page, choose a state change on an Obligation, such as Start or Resolve.

title: A revision keeps the history
annotation: The earlier version of the Obligation stays on record.

title: Revise an Obligation
annotation: Choose Revise on the Obligation and change its details.

title: Evidence records what the work produced
annotation: Evidence is a record of what the work produced. It is collected against a Deliverable.

title: Record Evidence
annotation: Open the Evidence tab of the SEU. Choose the Deliverable and the category, enter a title and the source, then choose Collect Evidence.

title: Evidence is checked before it is accepted
annotation: Each Evidence item is assessed on five dimensions: authenticity, completeness, consistency, source credibility and engineering relevance. The assessments set the confidence of the Evidence.

title: Validate the Evidence
description: Assess the Evidence on a dimension.
annotation: On the Evidence tab, choose a dimension and a status (Pass, Partial, Fail or Not Assessed) in the row of the Evidence, then choose Assess.

title: Evidence has a lifecycle
annotation: Accepted Evidence helps a Deliverable pass the Quality Gate from Approved to Baselined.

title: Move the Evidence on
description: Move the Evidence to its next state.
annotation: In the Transition column of the Evidence row, choose one of the buttons offered, such as Accept or Reject.

title: Links show what the Evidence supports
annotation: A link connects the Evidence to a Deliverable it supports.

title: Link the Evidence
description: Link the Evidence to a Deliverable.
annotation: In the Link another column of the Evidence row, select a Deliverable and choose Link.

title: Knowledge keeps what the unit has learned
annotation: A Knowledge item records a lesson or a reusable finding from the work.

title: Record a Knowledge item
annotation: Choose Record Knowledge, enter the details and save.

title: Knowledge is reviewed before it is shared
description: Move the Knowledge item on - note
annotation: A Knowledge item is proposed, validated, accepted and then published.

title: Move the Knowledge item on
description: Move the Knowledge item to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Knowledge item, such as Propose or Publish.

title: Scope decides who can see the Knowledge
annotation: Promotion widens the Knowledge from the unit to a wider audience.

title: Promote the Knowledge item
description: Promote the Knowledge item to a wider scope.
annotation: Choose Promote scope on the Knowledge item.

title: Knowledge Capital is the organisation's shared learning
annotation: It collects published Knowledge from every unit.

title: Open Knowledge Capital
annotation: In the navbar, open Knowledge Capital. It lists the Knowledge the organisation has gathered.

title: A Decision records a choice and its reason
annotation: A Decision stays with the unit so that the reason for a choice can be found later.

title: Record a Decision
annotation: Choose Record Decision, enter the details and save.

title: A Decision is reviewed and approved
annotation: A Decision is analysed, proposed, reviewed, approved and applied.

title: Move the Decision on
description: Move the Decision to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Decision, such as Review or Approve.

title: External parties are part of the work
annotation: An external interaction records a request to or a reply from a party outside the unit.

title: Record an external interaction
annotation: Choose Record interaction, enter the details and save.

title: An interaction has a lifecycle
annotation: The interaction moves from requested to answered to closed.

title: Move the interaction on
description: Move the external interaction to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the interaction.

title: A review examines the work
annotation: A review checks a Deliverable or a stage of the work and records what it finds.

title: Open the reviews
description: Open the reviews of the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, open Reviews.

title: A review has a subject
annotation: The review is opened against the work it examines.

title: Start a review
annotation: Choose Start review and select what is reviewed.

title: A review ends with an outcome
annotation: The review is completed when its findings are recorded.

title: Move the review on
description: Move the review to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the review.

title: A Finding records a problem found
annotation: A Finding states what is wrong and how serious it is.

title: Raise a Finding
description: Raise a Finding in the review.
annotation: In the review, choose Raise Finding, enter the details and save.

title: A Finding is handled until it is closed
annotation: A Finding is accepted, resolved or dismissed.

title: Move the Finding on
description: Move the Finding to its next state.
annotation: Choose a state change on the Finding.

title: A Finding can become work
description: Convert the Finding into an Obligation - note
annotation: Converting a Finding creates an Obligation, so that the fix is tracked to closure.

title: Convert the Finding into an Obligation
description: Convert the Finding into an Obligation.
annotation: Choose Convert on the Finding.

title: Attention items flag what needs notice
annotation: An Attention Item flags something that needs notice. One that blocks progress holds its Deliverable until it is resolved.

title: Raise an Attention item
annotation: On the unit page, open the Attention Items tab. Choose the Deliverable, or SEU-level, enter the category and the title, choose the priority and choose Create Attention Item.

title: An Attention item is cleared by a person
description: Move the Attention item on - note
annotation: Resolving an Attention Item that blocks progress lets the work continue.

title: Move the Attention item on
description: Resolve, release or waive an Attention item on the SEU.
annotation: On the Attention Items tab, choose a button in the Transition column of the item, such as Resolve.

title: Attention gathers items from every unit
annotation: One list shows what needs notice across the organisation.

title: Open Attention across units
annotation: In the navbar, open Attention. The list shows the items of every unit.

title: The list works like the unit page
description: Move an Attention item from the list - note
annotation: The same state changes are available from the list.

title: Move an Attention item from the list
description: Move an Attention item from the Attention list.
annotation: On the Attention list, choose a state change on an item.

title: Compliance is the state of the Obligations
annotation: The view shows how far the unit has met what the Engineering Behavior Model requires.

title: Open the compliance view
description: Open the compliance view of the SEU.
annotation: On the unit page, open Compliance. It shows which Obligations are met and which are open.

title: A waiver excuses an Obligation
annotation: A waiver is recorded with a reason, by a person with the authority to excuse it.

title: Record a waiver
annotation: On the compliance view, choose Waive on an Obligation, enter the reason and save.

title: The dashboard summarises the platform
annotation: It shows the counts and states that matter at a glance.

title: Open the dashboard
annotation: In the navbar, open the Dashboard. It summarises the state of the units.

title: Telemetry shows how the platform behaves
annotation: It reports counts and timings of what the platform does.

title: Open Telemetry
annotation: In the navbar, open Telemetry.

title: Every change publishes an event
annotation: Events record what happened, who did it and with which badge.

title: Open Events
annotation: In the navbar, open Events.

title: Version events record each version
annotation: A version event is recorded when an entity reaches a new version.

title: Open Version Events
annotation: In the navbar, open Version Events.

title: The Deliverables tab shows the work in execution
description: Deliverables tab of an SEU - note
annotation: The Deliverables tab lists every Deliverable of the unit with its state. For each one it shows the Quality Gate items that apply to its next hop, the Quality Gate Outcome, the Attention items, the participants and the transition that is blocked.

title: Open the Deliverables tab
description: Open the Deliverables tab of an SEU.
annotation: Use the Modified Demo Profile for ArchVault Team to commission the SEU, then open it from SEU Platform and All SEUs. Stay on the Deliverables tab. Each row is a Deliverable with its state, the Quality Gate items of its next hop, the Quality Gate Outcome, the Attention items, the participants and the blocked transition.

title: Why Requirements Analysis Model is blocked
description: Read why the Quality Gate is Blocked.
annotation: Requirements Analysis Model is in the Defined state, and the No Unresolved Obligations Quality Gate governs the hop from Defined to In Progress. The Demo False Trigger Policy raised the Obligation "Resolve the Demo False Trigger Policy" for this Deliverable. The Obligation is still open, so the Quality Gate Outcome is Blocked and the In Progress button stays disabled.

title: Why the other Deliverables are not decided
description: Read why the Quality Gate is Not decided.
annotation: The Quality Gate Outcome shows Not decided yet for Source Code and Deployment Manifest. No decision is stored for their hop yet. Both Deliverables depend on Requirements Analysis Model, so their decision waits on that Deliverable.

title: Check whether a Policy raised an Obligation or Attention Item
description: Find the Obligation or Attention Item of a Policy.
annotation: Read the Attention items column of the Deliverable row. Open the Obligations tab and the Attention Items tab of the SEU to see each record, its Deliverable and its status. Open the Quality Gates tab. Under Blocked now each blocked line states why it blocks.

title: Progress is unblocked by resolution or by a waiver
annotation: A blocked hop is unblocked in one of two ways. Resolve the Obligations and Attention Items that hold it, or grant a waiver for the Obligation or the Quality Gate line that blocks it.

title: Grant the waivers
description: Waive the Obligation and the Quality Gate.
annotation: Open the SEU and choose the Quality Gates tab. Under Blocked now are the Obligation "Resolve the Demo False Trigger Policy" and the No Unresolved Obligations Quality Gate line. Choose Grant waiver on the Obligation line, enter a rationale and save. Choose Grant waiver again, pick the No Unresolved Obligations Quality Gate line, enter a rationale and save.

title: See the Deliverables move
annotation: Reload the SEU and open the Deliverables tab. Requirements Analysis Model has moved to In Progress. The Quality Gate of Deployment Manifest is now checked, because the Deliverable dependency it waits on is met. The Quality Gate itself still blocks the move to the next state until its own conditions are met or waived.

title: The demo participants view mocks what a Human participant sees
annotation: The Demo participants view is a mock of the page an actual Human participant gets to see. It also shows a sample response from an AI participant.

title: Open the Demo participants view
annotation: In the navbar, open SEU Platform, then Demo Participants. Choose a Human participant in the list. The page shows what that participant sees, and every action runs as that participant.

title: Provide Evidence
annotation: On the Deliverables tab of the participant page, choose the Actions of a Deliverable and then Provide Evidence. Pick the category, enter a title and save. The Evidence is listed on the Evidence tab.

title: Create Knowledge
annotation: Choose the Actions of a Deliverable and then Create Knowledge. Select the supporting Evidence, enter the category and title, and save. Knowledge always cites the Evidence it rests on.

title: Create a Decision
description: Create a Decision as a participant.
annotation: Choose the Actions of a Deliverable and then Create Decision. Enter the title, add the alternatives, select the supporting Knowledge or Evidence, and save.

title: An AI participant responds through the same page
annotation: An AI participant does its work through the same records a Human participant uses. The Work Item Instructions provides the required Prompts/Skills for the AI agent to work within the governed environment.

title: View the AI response
annotation: Open Demo Participants and choose an AI participant, for example ArchVault Analysis Agent. The response is the Evidence, Knowledge, Decision and Attention Items the agent recorded, listed on the matching tabs. The status it reported on the Command / Work Item tab. Choose Instructions there to read what the agent was asked to do.
